claim: The new ERP_RIDER_SHARE table gives RydePOOL the default share 1.0 and says 'all other services exclude ERP from the fare, so the rider pays the ERP'. Ryde's own articles in the corpus say each RydePOOL rider pays 50% of the toll (and an older note says RydePOOL fares include ERP). The table, FC-F04 and the engine therefore decide a RydePOOL ERP dispute at the full-ERP default, automatically, on an A-rated source.
how: ERP_RIDER_SHARE now has a share only for the services Ryde's 2026-09-02 driver article names; RydePOOL, RydeHIRE, Ryde X GO, Ryde+ and RydeSEND-plus-carpool go to GEN-R07, a missing service type to FC-R12 (rules FC-R06, FC-F04, table note, T19 to T22); D35 and O15 widened

claim: FC-R08's new cap ('with FC-R07 the refund never exceeds the ERP charged to the rider') is not in the task, and it still over-refunds when the rider was charged less than ERP(actual). The engine refunds min(ERP(actual) - ERP(recommended), charged) even when the rider paid no more than the recommended route would have cost. The reason codes also contradict the outcome when nothing is charged.
how: FC-R08 refund is now min(ERP(actual), ERP charged) minus ERP(recommended), floor 0, FC-R07 on top; engine, PB step note, D35 and tests T23 to T25 changed

claim: The G3 test does not pin the AUTH-04 statement, the text the Judge and reviewers read. It only checks the gate_tiers data field and that the same gate IDs appear in the statement, so reverting the prose to the old behavior still passes.
how: rule_card_check now tests the AUTH-04 prose (G3 in the APPROVE sentence, not in the no-single-ruling sentence, provisional ruling = history-blind) and a mutant shows it fails

claim: FC-F03's new GPS justification carries an extra condition that is neither Ryde text nor labeled as FairRyde's: it counts only if 'shown by the trip's navigation record'. The KB has no such evidence item, so in practice the justification can only be supported by a driver statement, which the same sentence ranks as tier C.
how: FC-F03: navigation record labeled as FairRyde's evidence rule (source entry and note), bare statement does not establish it (GEN-R01), tier C or D, zh fixed

claim: FC-R01's new exception says generally 'a fixed fare does not include ERP (FC-F01)', which contradicts FC-R06 for RydeSEND (fares include ERP). The step's own precedence (FC-R06 first) is not reflected in FC-R01, so a RydeSEND route ticket with extra gantries opens an FC-TOLL claim that can only end in 'nothing to refund'.
how: FC-R01 names the RydeSEND exception (FC-R06), en and zh

claim: The new table ERP_RIDER_SHARE, and FC-R06, FC-F04 and FC-R07 on top of it, are rated A with a default share of 1.0 for 'every other service'. The cited article does not say that, and other Ryde pages contradict it for RydePOOL and RydeHIRE. The conflict is not in META-04's known_conflicts or in D35, and the engine treats RydePOOL, RydeHIRE and an unrecorded service type as share 1.0.
how: same as A2-F1; the A rating of FC-R06, FC-F04 and the table now holds because every share is from the 2026-09-02 article; no META-04 known-conflict entry added (recorded in D35 and O15)

claim: FC-R07 is rated A, but its remedy ('refund the difference') has no Ryde source. Ryde's quoted clause only says an excessive ERP amount is fraudulent. D32 keeps FC-R07 for METERED fares only on the ground that 'it rests on Ryde's driver article, which covers RydeTAXI', which supports the fraud clause and not a platform-computed refund. D32's own reasons for excluding FC-R08 (Ryde publishes no refund rule for a metered fare; payment is cash only) apply equally to this refund.
how: FC-R07 got a FAIRRYDE source and a credibility note saying the refund is FairRyde's remedy; the rating stays A in A2 and is left to Jasper (D35 item 5, recommended D in A3); the metered refund is kept and its reason recorded in D32

claim: FC-F03's GPS justification drops the fixed-fare premise of both Ryde sentences, is applied to FC-TOLL and to METERED trips where that premise fails, and leaves the rule at C on the reasoning that it 'stays C because of its DiDi element'. Under the credibility_principle (weakest essential element; a Ryde condition extended by FairRyde is D) the extension would be D. A3's census is planned to relabel B and C rules, and D36 records the tension, so this is outcome-neutral (FC-F03 is READ and decisive either way).
how: FC-F03 stays C; the credibility note and D35 item 4 say that Ryde states the permission for fixed fares so using it for ERP claims extends it; A3's census rates it

claim: FC-F03 says a bare driver statement 'is tier C evidence'. The KB's own scale puts a free-text statement (including the driver's response) at tier D, and tier C is party-generated but system-recorded (chat, photos). GEN-R04 says 'tier C or D'. The zh text says 口头说明 (an oral statement) for 'bare statement'. The required 'trip's navigation record' has no evidence type and is in no playbook's required_evidence.
how: same as A2-F4 (tier C or D, zh text)

claim: FC-R01's new exception is not fully labeled and slightly overstated: the note says the opening of an FC-TOLL claim 'follows from' CLS-02 although CLS-02 is 'one claim per contested charge' and the rider has not contested the ERP; the card has no FAIRRYDE source or D35 pointer for this FairRyde design (D35(2) is 'to confirm with Jasper'); 'a fixed fare does not include ERP' omits the RydeSEND exception, and its source is a RydeX-only page. The rule stays B. Outcome-neutral because FC-R08 applies FC-R06 first, so RydeSEND gets 0; A3's census will relabel B rules.
how: FC-R01 got a FAIRRYDE source for opening the claim unasked, the note no longer says CLS-02 supports it; D35 item 2

claim: FC-R07's zh text omits the TOLL_TOLERANCE_SGD condition that the English has, and the card does not mention that the carpool comparison basis (the ERP line the rider was charged against the rider's 50%) rests on the unanswered question O15 / D35(1), although the rule is rated A.

claim: FC-R08's PDVL-only note is not reflected in its scope. It applies to every non-METERED trip, including RydeX trips that Ryde says may be served by a taxi driver and carpool trips (share 0.5) whose drivers are not PDVL holders, where the cited LTA duty is not verified. D32 excludes RydeTAXI on exactly this ground but leaves these. PB-FC-TOLL.sources does not list LTA-PDVL-OFFENCES, RYDE-4412121982745 or RYDE-4412122016153, which FC-F03 and FC-R08 use. The D rating already forces approval, so this is outcome-neutral.
how: FC-R08 says it does not check the driver type (taxi driver on RydeX, carpool driver); LTA-PDVL-OFFENCES and the route articles added to PB-FC-TOLL sources; D35 item 3

claim: The CW-F06 source note still says the reading is frozen and later steps do not extend it, and does not mention the D38 exception that A2 made in the engine. claim: frozen area (D34): the same hazard as limitation 1 remains for 'office' (and house, room). 'I'm at the office' reads LATE, so an automatic uphold is possible when the pick-up is an office building. D38 lists these words as 'unchanged' but does not record them as a known limitation.
how: frozen area (D34); D38 lists office, house, home, work, room and so on as unchanged for Jasper to decide

claim: When the refund is capped to zero because the rider was charged no ERP, the engine returns UPHOLD with two contradictory reason codes (FC-R-TOLL-FROM-DETOUR, whose taxonomy outcome is TOLL_REFUND, and FC-R-TOLL-VALID) and keeps FC-F03 decisive although the amount cannot change, so the tier is APPROVE instead of AUTO. The rule cards do not say what the outcome is in this case.
how: FC-R-TOLL-FROM-DETOUR only when the detour refund is above 0; FC-F03 decisive only when the amount can change; reason and outcome consistency now a build check (erp_code_check); T25

claim: The labels of two ERP reason codes still describe the old plain-gantry-sum behavior and are false for the new exceptions.

claim: FC-R08's cap 'the refund never exceeds the ERP charged' is the wrong cap. When the rider was charged less than the actual path's ERP (for example only the recommended route's ERP), the rule and engine refund up to the whole charged line, so the rider ends with less than the ERP the recommended route would have cost. Because FC-R01 now opens this claim proactively, this is the likely case on every route ticket where the platform charged the estimated ERP. In addition, a zero refund carries contradictory reason codes.
how: same as A2-F2 (CRITICAL after the skeptic: the cap refunded money owed on the recommended route)
